title: Electricity Production and Exchange 5 min Realtime
description: The electricity production and exchange in MW in 5 minutes intervals and updated every 5 minutes.
comment:
**NOTE:** Data are based on upscaled real-time power measurements from the SCADA system. **Errors will occur, and will generally not be corrected.** For statistical purposes, see [Production and Consumption - Settlement](https://www.energidataservice.dk/tso-electricity/ProductionConsumptionSettlement).

The total load, including loses, is calculated as the sum of production from power plants, solar and wind power plus the exchange to Germany, Sweden, Norway, and The Netherlands. The exchange between Bornholm and Price area SE4 is included in the exchange DK2 to Sweden, and should not be taken into account.

---
**API Request Frequency** \
To get the most up-to-date data, calling the API with a dynamic timestamp such as [start=now-PT15M](https://api.energidataservice.dk/dataset/ElectricityProdex5MinRealtime?start=now-PT15M) is a good approach. Making a request every few minutes or so is sufficient to ensure getting the latest data.
caution:
* Erroneous values occur in the column 'Production on plants less than 100 MW' from 2026-03-30 10.00 to 10.15 CET. The values will not be corrected.

* Due to technical issues the switch to Daylight Saving Time (DST) has caused erroneous values to occur between 2026-03-29 03.00 and 04.00 CET. The values will not be corrected.
author: Energinet

columns.description: UTC timestamp at which the values are valid.
columns.comment:
Please note that the _format_ shown in the example applies to data downloaded as JSON or fetched through the API.
The format is slightly different when it is shown on screen or downloaded manually as CSV or XLSX. This is mainly due to readability and consideration for Excel users.

**In preview (in the GUI)** all timestamps are shown as (display convention)
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mmZ
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:05Z. 
The Z will remind viewers that this is UTC.

In **download (CSV and XLSX)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:05.
That is without the “T” and the “Z” and the seconds. Excel will recognize it as date-time. The user must remember the convention about time zones.

In **download (JSON and API)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss
e.g. 2017-07-14T08:05:00.
columns.validationRules: Always full minutes, i.e. seconds are 00

columns.description: Timestamp (in the _Danish time zone_) at which the values are valid.
columns.comment:
On one normal day there will be 24 * 12 = 288 intervals.

When daylight saving times shifts there will be either 276 or 300 intervals.

Please note that the _format_ shown in the example applies to data downloaded as JSON or fetched through the API.
The format is slightly different when it is shown on screen or downloaded manually as CSV or XLSX. This is mainly due to readability and consideration for Excel users.

**In preview (in the GUI)** all timestamps are shown as (display convention)
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:05. 
Please note that there is no time zone indicator, showing that this is local (Danish) time.

In **download (CSV and XLSX)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:05.
That is without the “T” and the seconds. Excel will recognize it as date-time. The user must remember that this is local (Danish) time.

In **download (JSON and API)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss
e.g. 2017-07-14T08:05:00.
columns.validationRules: Always full minutes, i.e. seconds are 00

columns.description: Same as bidding zone. Denmark is divided in two price areas (bidding zones) divided by the Great Belt. DK1 is west of the Great Belt and DK2 is east of the Great Belt.
columns.comment: Some datasets contain a limited number of price areas.
columns.validationRules: DK1, DK2, DE, NO2, SE3, SE4

columns.description: Production on plants with a capacity greater than or equal to 100MW. Data based on energy measurements.
Electricity production from offshore wind power.
columns.comment: Includes both large offshore parks like Horns reef, and local wind turbines located offshore.

columns.description: Electricity production from onshore wind power.
columns.comment: All wind generators that are not specifically registrered as off-shore wind generators.

The estimated production is based on real-time measurements, occasionally containing small errors that are not corrected retroactively. Consequently, these estimates may deviate from actual production, such as instances of minimal nighttime solar panel output.
